tip: 그치다 (geuchida) = (rain or snow) stops: 비가 그쳤어요 (biga geuchyeosseoyo).
-씩 (-ssik) = bit by bit: 조금씩 (jogeumssik) = little by little.
비를 맞다 (bireul matda) = get rained on – you "receive" the rain.
천둥이 치다 (cheondungi chida) = thunder "strikes" in Korean.
-고 있어요 (-go isseoyo) = is ...ing right now: 오고 있어요 (ogo isseoyo) = is coming.
-(으)ㄹ 거예요 (-l geoyeyo) = will, is going to: 올 거예요 (ol geoyeyo) = it will come.
With -아서 (-aseo) only the last verb takes past tense: 비가 와서 축구를 취소했어요 (biga waseo chukgureul chwisohaesseoyo). 와서 (waseo) stays tense-free even though the rain already fell.
Snow 'comes' in Korean: 첫눈이 왔어요 (cheonnuni wasseoyo = the first snow came). Rain too – 비가 와요 (biga wayo = it rains). There is no single verb 'to snow' or 'to rain'.
Korean describes how with sound-words: 눈이 펑펑 와요 (nuni peongpeong wayo) – 펑펑 (peongpeong) is fat snowflakes falling thick. Rain pours 주룩주룩 (jurukjuruk).
몇 도예요? (myeot doyeyo) = how many degrees? Temperatures use the 일, 이, 삼 (il, i, sam) number set: 오 도 (o do) = 5 degrees.
끼다 (kkida) = wear things that slide on: gloves, rings, glasses. 장갑을 꼈어요 (janggabeul kkyeosseoyo).
목도리를 하다 (mokdorireul hada) = scarves are usually "done", not "worn".
날씨가 풀리다 (nalssiga pullida) = the cold "loosens" when a freeze ends.
-기 시작하다 (-gi sijakhada) = start doing: 피기 시작했어요 (pigi sijakhaesseoyo) = started to bloom. The -기 (-gi) turns the verb into a noun the starting attaches to.
-(으)ㄹ 때 (-l ttae) = when doing: 나갈 때 (nagal ttae) = when going out.
잠이 안 와요 (jami an wayo) = sleep "won't come", meaning you can't fall asleep.
-고 싶어요 (-go sipeoyo) = want to: 가고 싶어요 (gago sipeoyo) = I want to go.
Koreans praise fall skies as "high": 하늘이 높아요 (haneuri nopayo).
단풍이 들다 (danpungi deulda) = leaves "take on" their fall colors.
Koreans call fall 독서의 계절 (dokseo-e gyejeol) = the reading season.
중에서 (jungeseo) after a noun = among: 사계절 중에서 (sagyejeol jungeseo) = among the four seasons.
뜨다 (tteuda) = rise, come up: 무지개가 떴어요 (mujigaega tteosseoyo) = a rainbow came up. Sun and moon use the same verb.
The sun 지다 (jida = sets) and 뜨다 (tteuda = rises) in Korean: 해가 일찍 져요 (haega iljjik jyeoyo) = the sun sets early. Same verbs work for the moon.
할머니 (halmeoni) takes respect forms: 타세요 (taseyo) – the 세 (se) is the respect marker 시 (si) merged into the -어요 (-eoyo) ending.
더위를 타다 (deowireul tada) = "ride" the heat, meaning you feel it badly. Cold uses the same verb: 추위를 타다 (chuwireul tada).
Answer with a noun + 이에요 (ieyo): 제 취미는 등산이에요 (je chwimineun deungsan-ieyo) = my hobby is hiking.
Words like 조용하다 (joyonghada = be quiet) add -ㄴ/은 before a noun: 조용한 취미 (joyonghan chwimi) = a quiet hobby.
-(으)면 (-myeon) = if: 취미가 있으면 (chwimiga isseumyeon) = if you have a hobby.
-(으)ㄹ까요? (-lkkayo) = shall we? 같이 등산할까요? (gachi deungsanhalkkayo) = shall we hike together?
후에 (hue) = after: 등산 후에 (deungsan hue) = after hiking. 막걸리 (makgeolli) is the classic post-hike reward.
